title: Identifiability of Parent User
description: Registration data includes PII (email, name, government ID) that directly identifies the parent user, making them identifiable to the authentication service and any parties with access to this data.
assumptions: Standard registration flow where PII is transmitted to authentication service

title: Disclosure of Sensitive Registration Data
description: Sensitive data (password, government ID, six-digit code) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or if the authentication service is compromised.
assumptions: Data transmitted over network and stored in authentication service

title: Data Aggregation with Other User Information
description: Authentication service could aggregate registration data with other data about the parent user (e.g., usage patterns, other accounts), creating a more complete profile.
assumptions: Authentication service has access to or can link with other data stores

title: Unawareness of Data Collection Scope
description: Parent user may not be fully aware of what data is being collected, how it will be used, or who has access to their registration information.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not be clearly communicated or understood during registration

title: Unintended Recipients of Registration Data
description: Registration data could be accessed by unintended recipients such as third-party services, other system components, or unauthorized personnel within the organization.
assumptions: Authentication service may share data with other systems or have access controls that could be bypassed

title: Excessive data collection in parent account storage
description: The Authentication Service may store more personal data than necessary when saving parent account information to MongoDB, violating the data minimality principle. This could include unnecessary fields, historical data, or metadata that exceeds what is required for authentication purposes.
assumptions: Parent account data contains personal information that should be minimized per privacy best practices

title: Linkability of parent account data with other system data
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB could be linked with other data stores or processes in the system, enabling creation of comprehensive user profiles beyond the original authentication purpose.
assumptions: Multiple data stores exist in the system that could be correlated

title: User unawareness of parent account data storage
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their parent account information is being stored in MongoDB, including what specific data elements are collected and for how long they are retained.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate data storage practices

title: Unauthorized interception of JWT and user data
description: The JWT token and user data transmitted from Authentication Service to Parent User could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing authentication credentials and personal information.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without guaranteed end-to-end encryption

title: Linkability of authentication data to user identity
description: The JWT and user data can be linked to identify the specific parent user, potentially enabling tracking of authentication activities across sessions or systems.
assumptions: JWT contains or can be correlated with user identifiers

title: Direct identifiability of parent user
description: User data sent to the parent user may contain personally identifiable information that directly reveals the user's identity.
assumptions: User data includes PII such as name, email, or user ID

title: Parent user unawareness of data processing
description: The parent user may not be fully aware of what data is being sent to them, how it will be used, or the privacy implications of receiving authentication tokens.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain data flows to external entities

title: Credential Disclosure in Transit
description: Parent email and password transmitted from child user to authentication service could be intercepted by network attackers, exposing sensitive authentication credentials.
assumptions: Data flow is not encrypted or uses weak encryption

title: Child Identifiability Through Parent Credentials
description: Child's identity can be linked to parent account through login credentials, potentially revealing child's activities and profile to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Authentication service maintains logs linking child sessions to parent accounts

title: Non-repudiation of Child Authentication
description: Child authenticating with parent credentials creates ambiguity about who performed the action - parent could deny authorizing child's login, or child could deny using credentials.
assumptions: No additional verification of actual user identity beyond credential submission

title: Child Privacy Regulation Compliance
description: Child authentication using parent credentials may not comply with child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA) requiring verifiable parental consent mechanisms.
assumptions: System does not implement additional parental consent verification beyond credential sharing
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements may vary by jurisdiction

title: Linkability of child authentication data
description: JWT containing userType 'child' combined with child profiles could enable linking of authentication events to specific child identities across sessions or services.
assumptions: JWT contains persistent identifiers or can be correlated with other data sources

title: Identifiability of child user
description: Child profiles transmitted to the child user may contain personally identifiable information that could expose the child's identity if intercepted or improperly accessed.
assumptions: Child profiles contain PII such as name, age, or other identifying attributes

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child data
description: Child profiles and JWT authentication tokens could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission from Authentication Service to child user.
assumptions: Transmission channel may not be properly secured or could be intercepted

title: Data aggregation enabling child profiling
description: JWT authentication data combined with child profiles could be aggregated with other data sources to create detailed behavioral profiles of the child.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that could be correlated with this flow's data

title: Child unawareness of data transmission
description: Child users may not be aware of what personal data (profiles, authentication tokens) is being transmitted to them or how it will be used.
assumptions: Child users lack full understanding of privacy implications of authentication flows

title: Non-compliance with child data protection regulations
description: Transmission of child profiles and authentication data may not comply with regulations like COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child-specific privacy requirements.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements exist for child data handling in the applicable jurisdiction
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory framework not specified in context

title: Child profile data enables cross-system linking
description: The combination of name, DOB, gender, and government ID transmitted in this flow creates powerful quasi-identifiers that could be used to link this child's profile with other data sources, enabling comprehensive profiling and tracking across systems.
assumptions: Government ID is a unique identifier; child data may exist in other systems

title: Sensitive child data exposed in transit
description: Personal information including government ID, date of birth, and name is transmitted from parent to system. If intercepted, this data could be used for identity theft or unauthorized profiling of the child.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network; encryption may or may not be in place

title: Child profile data could be modified in transit
description: An attacker could alter the child's information (name, DOB, gender, government ID) during transmission, leading to incorrect profile creation and potential downstream privacy and legal issues.
assumptions: Data integrity controls may not be fully implemented

title: Child data collection consent verification
description: The parent is creating a child's profile with sensitive data. There may be insufficient verification that the parent has proper legal authority to consent to this data collection on behalf of the child, or that the child's future consent rights are considered.
assumptions: System may not verify parental authority; child consent mechanisms may be inadequate
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and age of child - this is a general concern for child data flows

title: Unauthorized Access to Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be accessed by unauthorized parties if database access controls, authentication, or encryption are insufficient. This includes potential insider threats or external attackers exploiting vulnerabilities.
assumptions: MongoDB instance has standard security configurations; child profiles contain sensitive personal information

title: Excessive Data Collection in Child Profiles
description: The child profile management process may collect and store more personal data than necessary, violating the minimality principle. This could include unnecessary fields that increase privacy risk without providing proportional value.
assumptions: Child profile schema includes fields beyond what is strictly required for the application's purpose

title: Child Identifiability from Stored Profile
description: Child profile data may contain or enable identification of the child through direct identifiers (name, DOB) or indirect identifiers (unique combinations of attributes). If data is exposed, the child could be identified.
assumptions: Child profiles contain identifying information; data may be exposed through breach or improper access

title: Lack of Transparency About Data Storage
description: Parents or guardians may not be fully aware of what child profile data is being stored, how long it is retained, or how it is used. This lack of transparency prevents informed consent.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain data storage practices for child profiles

title: Non-compliance with Child Privacy Regulations
description: Child profile storage may not comply with applicable regulations (COPPA, GDPR-K, etc.) regarding consent, data minimization, retention limits, or parental rights. This creates legal and compliance risks.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdiction with child privacy regulations; compliance requirements may not be fully implemented

title: Linkability of child user activities to identity
description: Child user's video search queries, likes, and comments can be linked to their personal identity, creating a traceable activity profile that could be used to track the child's interests and behavior patterns.
assumptions: System maintains user accounts or session data that can associate activities with specific child users

title: Identifiability through behavioral patterns
description: Child user's identity may be revealed or inferred through their unique search patterns, content preferences (likes), and comment styles, even without explicit personal identifiers.
assumptions: Behavioral data is collected and stored with sufficient granularity to enable identification

title: Disclosure of personal information through content
description: Child users may inadvertently disclose personal information through their search queries, comments, or content preferences that could reveal sensitive details about their identity, location, or interests.
assumptions: Child users may not understand privacy implications of their interactions

title: Data aggregation creating child profiles
description: Video Management Service aggregates multiple data points from child users (search history, likes, comments) to build comprehensive behavioral profiles that could be used for targeted advertising or other purposes.
assumptions: Service retains and processes historical interaction data for profiling purposes

title: Unawareness of data collection scope
description: Child users may not be aware of the extent of data being collected about their search, like, and comment activities, or how this data will be used, stored, or shared.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not be age-appropriate or comprehensible to children

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Video Management Service may fail to comply with child-specific privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding data collection, consent, and processing of children's personal information.
assumptions: Service processes data from users under applicable age thresholds without proper safeguards
uncertainty_note: Citation Nc.2 from context [5] - Improper personal data management

title: Identified information in video metadata
description: Video metadata stored in MongoDB may contain identifying information such as user IDs, timestamps, device identifiers, or location data that could be used to identify individuals.
assumptions: Video metadata includes fields that can identify users or their activities

title: Implicit disclosure of personal data through video storage
description: Storing video files and metadata in MongoDB may result in implicit disclosure of personal data, especially if videos contain identifiable individuals or sensitive information that was not explicitly intended for storage.
assumptions: Videos may contain personally identifiable information or sensitive content

title: Linkability of video data across contexts
description: Video metadata and content stored in this flow could be linked with other data sources to build comprehensive profiles of individuals, enabling tracking across different contexts.
assumptions: Video data can be correlated with other system data

title: Excessive child data storage
description: Child search and watch history is being stored in the database, which may exceed the minimality principle. This data collection may be more than strictly necessary for the system's core functionality, representing implicit data disclosure.
assumptions: System stores detailed search and watch history for child profiles

title: Lack of awareness about data collection
description: Children and parents may not be aware that their search and watch history is being stored in the database. This lack of transparency prevents informed consent about what personal data is being collected.
assumptions: No explicit notification or consent mechanism for storing search/watch history

title: Potential non-compliance with child data protection regulations
description: Storing child search and watch history may not comply with child-specific privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) which require special protections for children's personal data and strict data minimization.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdiction with child data protection laws
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation details

title: Linkability of child activity data
description: Stored search and watch history could be linked to identify specific children, especially when combined with other data sources. This creates linkability risks for child profiles.
assumptions: Child profile data contains or can be associated with identifying information

title: Video uploads linkable to parent identity
description: Video uploads from parent users can be linked to their specific identity/account, enabling correlation of uploaded content with the parent's profile and other data.
assumptions: System maintains user accounts and associates uploads with parent identities

title: Parent identifiable through video upload activity
description: Parent users are identifiable when uploading videos, as the system records who uploaded what content and when.
assumptions: System authenticates and identifies parent users during upload

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video content
description: Video content uploaded by parents could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during upload, processing, or storage in the video management service.
assumptions: Video content may contain sensitive personal information about children or families

title: Parent unaware of data processing scope
description: Parents may not be fully aware of what data is collected during video upload, how it's processed, who has access, or retention periods.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Video upload and approval process may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR) regarding children's data and parental consent.
assumptions: Videos may contain children's data requiring special protection
uncertainty_note: Context suggests video content may involve children, but specific regulatory requirements not confirmed

title: Child Identifiability Through Video Stream
description: The video management service may identify the specific child user through the streaming session, potentially linking viewing activity to the child's identity. This could occur through account association, device fingerprinting, or session tracking.
assumptions: The video management service maintains user accounts or session tracking for child users

title: Viewing Profile Aggregation
description: Multiple video streams to the child could be aggregated to build a detailed profile of the child's viewing preferences, habits, and interests. This aggregated data could be used for behavioral profiling or targeted content delivery.
assumptions: The system tracks and stores viewing history across multiple sessions

title: Unawareness of Data Collection During Streaming
description: The child or their guardians may not be fully aware of what data is collected during video streaming (e.g., viewing duration, device information, interaction patterns). This lack of transparency prevents informed consent.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data collection practices during video streaming

title: Non-compliance with Children's Privacy Regulations
description: Streaming video to children may violate regulations like COPPA if proper parental consent, data minimization, or age-appropriate safeguards are not implemented. The flow may collect or process data in ways that don't comply with children's privacy laws.
assumptions: The system may not have adequate COPPA compliance measures for child users
uncertainty_note: Citation based on general knowledge of children's privacy regulations; specific compliance status unknown

title: Excessive child browsing data disclosure to AI engine
description: Child browsing data from the childprofiles collection is being transferred to the AI Recommendation Engine. This represents a data disclosure that may violate the minimality principle if not all transferred data is strictly required for the recommendation functionality. The planned nature of this flow raises questions about whether the data collection scope is appropriately limited.
assumptions: The childprofiles collection contains personal browsing data about children that is being sent to an AI processing system.

title: Child identifiability through browsing data transfer
description: Browsing data transferred from the childprofiles datastore to the AI engine may contain or enable identification of specific children. When combined with other data in the AI system, this could allow re-identification of individual children from their browsing patterns.
assumptions: The childprofiles collection contains data that can be linked to specific children, either directly or through quasi-identifiers.

title: Linkability of child browsing patterns across sessions
description: The transfer of child browsing data to the AI engine enables linking of browsing activities across different sessions and time periods, potentially creating comprehensive behavioral profiles of individual children that could be used for purposes beyond the original intent.
assumptions: The AI engine processes and stores browsing data in a way that allows correlation across multiple data points and time periods.

title: Unawareness of child data processing by AI engine
description: Children and their guardians may not be aware that browsing data is being transferred to an AI recommendation engine for processing. This lack of transparency about data flows and processing purposes violates the principle of informed consent.
assumptions: The data flow to the AI engine is not clearly communicated to users, or the purpose of AI processing is not adequately explained.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: Browsing data is explicitly transferred from the AI Recommendation Engine to Third-Party Advertisers. This represents an intentional disclosure of personal data across a system boundary to external parties. The minimality principle should be evaluated to ensure only strictly required data is shared.
assumptions: Browsing data contains personal information that can be linked to individual users

title: Linkability of Browsing Data with Advertiser Profiles
description: Third-party advertisers can link the received browsing data with other data they possess about users, creating comprehensive user profiles that enable targeted advertising and potential privacy violations.
assumptions: Advertisers maintain user profiles and can correlate incoming browsing data with existing records

title: User Unawareness of Data Sharing
description: Users may be unaware that their browsing data is being shared with third-party advertisers through the AI Recommendation Engine, limiting their ability to make informed consent decisions.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate third-party data sharing practices

title: Identifiability Through Browsing Patterns
description: Browsing data may contain unique patterns or combinations that can identify individual users, especially when combined with other data held by advertisers.
assumptions: Browsing data includes sufficient detail to enable user identification or re-identification

title: Linkability of government ID images to other personal data
description: Government ID images stored in the file system can be linked to other personal data about the individual, enabling comprehensive profiling. The Authentication Service may correlate ID images with authentication logs, user profiles, or other system data.
assumptions: System maintains other personal data that could be correlated with stored ID images

title: Identifiability through stored government ID images
description: Government ID images contain inherently identifying information (photos, names, ID numbers, dates of birth). Storage in the file system makes this data directly identifiable to the individual.
assumptions: ID images contain standard government identification elements

title: Unauthorized disclosure of government ID images
description: If the file system (backend/uploads/) is compromised or improperly secured, government ID images could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to identity theft or fraud.
assumptions: File system has potential security vulnerabilities or access control gaps

title: Excessive data disclosure through ID image storage
description: Storing government ID images may violate the minimality principle if such storage is not strictly necessary for the authentication service's function. This represents an avoidable disclosure of highly sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Alternative authentication methods might not require storing full ID images
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether ID image storage is truly necessary for the authentication process

title: User unawareness of ID image storage
description: Users may not be aware that their government ID images are being stored, where they are stored, for how long, or who has access to them. This lack of transparency prevents informed consent.
assumptions: Privacy policy or user interface does not clearly communicate ID image storage practices

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Storing government ID images may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, local privacy laws) regarding special category data, data minimization, or storage limitations.
assumptions: Applicable regulations restrict storage of government identification documents
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory requirements depend on jurisdiction

title: JWT enables cross-session user activity linking
description: JWT stored in localStorage contains user identity information that can be used to link user activities across different sessions, pages, or time periods, enabling behavioral tracking and profiling.
assumptions: JWT contains user identifiers and is accessible to scripts on the same domain

title: JWT exposes user identity in client-side storage
description: Storing JWT in localStorage makes user identity information accessible to browser scripts, potentially exposing identifying information to malicious code or unauthorized parties through XSS attacks.
assumptions: JWT contains user identifying information and localStorage is accessible to JavaScript

title: JWT disclosure through client-side storage vulnerabilities
description: JWT stored in localStorage can be disclosed to unauthorized parties through XSS attacks, browser extensions, or other client-side vulnerabilities that can read localStorage contents.
assumptions: Application may be vulnerable to XSS or other client-side attacks

title: Users unaware of JWT storage implications
description: Users are typically unaware that their authentication tokens are stored in browser localStorage and the privacy implications of this storage mechanism, including potential tracking and data exposure risks.
assumptions: No explicit user consent or notification about localStorage usage for authentication

title: Unauthorized Information Disclosure of Child History
description: Child history data retrieved and sent to parent may contain sensitive information that should not be disclosed, such as behavioral patterns, location history, or personal interactions that could compromise the child's privacy.
assumptions: Child history contains potentially sensitive personal data; parent access may not be fully appropriate for all data types

title: Linking of Child History with Other Data Sources
description: Child history data sent to parent could be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, medical data, social media) to build a comprehensive profile of the child, revealing additional information beyond what was intended to be shared.
assumptions: Parent may have access to or ability to correlate with other child-related data sources

title: Data Theft During Transmission
description: Child history data could be intercepted and stolen during transmission from the Child Profile Management process to the Parent User, exposing sensitive child information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or secured

title: Unauthorized Access to Child History Data
description: Unauthorized parties could gain access to child history data during the flow from process to parent, potentially through compromised credentials or system vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Authentication and authorization controls may have weaknesses
